Whether the fungal infections arose from pre-existing colonisation or secondary to immunosuppression is a hedged author interpretation
Authors state the MIC data cannot be directly translated into clinical treatment decisions
The breed or name-like word after female intact is not defined in the source

limitations: Single-dog report; the article gives no dates, only relative times (48 weeks of therapy, four weeks later).
The word following 'female intact' in the case text is not interpreted or stored.
Dose of the prednisolone increase, duration of antifungal therapy and the interval to euthanasia are not stated.
Susceptibility results are author-stated MICs without interpretive breakpoints; the authors caution against translating them into treatment decisions.

Figure 1 panel C pixels show orange to brown colonies while the caption states light purple pigmentation; caption text is kept and the discrepancy is recorded in the visual limitations and ambiguities.
Discussion statements about published cases, cohorts and recommendations were not copied to the dog.
The source has no tables and no supplements.

Histology showed severe pyogranulomatous deep dermatitis with intralesional conidia in nasal tissue and septated hyphae in tail tissue. Culture and ITS PCR identified Purpureocillium sodanum in the tail lesions and Alternaria rosae in the nasal lesions, and EUCAST microdilution MICs were measured.
